title: YourSpecialist
description:
Medical Locator site project. I used React, Vite, React Router, HTML, SCSS, JS, local data base.

I plan for this project to add the SQL database from which I will filter the information and from which I will retrieve information about the availability of each doctor in the database. And after that I will do the modularization of the components from scratch to be able to organize, set and reuse them.
Plus I will correct the mistake in SCSS in which I ranked the code, being a good habit.

title: Stock Document Management
description:
Stock Doc Management is a web application for investors who want to manage their stock portfolios in one place. It keeps track of transactions, deposited and withdrawn money, investment theses, dividends and the financial operations specific to brokerage platforms, such as interest on free funds, corrections and platform fees.

The application automatically calculates profit and performance, generates customizable and filterable charts and tables, and helps you make decisions based on your own investment theses and on news about the companies in your portfolio, instead of Excel files that are hard to maintain and follow. Portfolio data can be exported to customizable files, and backups are easy to make. Investors spend less time searching and filtering data, generating reports and following their investment theses and market news. On top of that, they can adapt the portfolio to their own strategy.

I have been working on this project for a while and I have reached the point where I want to publish it and find people interested in the subject who would like to use the application. Below are the application's features, together with a few representative images. This is a technical overview of the project.

Accounts and security

I started with the accounts. On registration, the account is not created until the user confirms their email address with an 8-digit code received by email, valid for 30 seconds. A new code can only be requested after the old one expires. Changing the password works the same way: the approval code is sent to the account's email, and the new password cannot be one the account has ever had before. Passwords and codes are never stored in plain text, only as hashes. For "forgot password" the validation process is the same, and the application's response is identical whether or not the email address has an account. I did this so that nobody can find out which emails are registered in the database.

Portfolios

Users can create a portfolio with the name and currency they want. A portfolio can use multiple brokerage accounts that share the same currency. The application presents the information for each account individually, as well as for all accounts together, with several display modes, so every user can follow them in the way that is easiest for them.

Pages

The Home page contains:

  • the main portfolio KPIs;
  • the alerts generated by active investment theses;
  • analyst price analysis, both summarized by Yahoo Finance and detailed: which analysts covered each stock and in which periods, from the data provided by the Yahoo Finance financial API;
  • the calendar with the earnings dates of the companies in the portfolio, stock splits and news about the companies held.

The Portfolio page gathers everything that matters about the portfolio: KPIs, closed and open positions, dividends and other brokerage platform operations, plus various charts presenting the portfolio information. The information can be filtered by period, by account (if the user has multiple brokerage accounts in the same currency) and by position status: open, closed or both. It can be displayed grouped by account, for example all the information about Account 1, then everything about Account 2, or interleaved: the KPIs for Account 1, then the KPIs for Account 2 and so on. This page also generates a PDF report in which you can customize the colors of the values in charts and tables, reorder sections and charts, rename sections, columns and charts, and choose the column order in tables and which columns appear.

The Analytics page offers all the charts of a stock, with the portfolio positions marked on them, plus adjacent charts for indicators (EMA 20, SMA 50, SMA 200, RSI 14, MACD etc.) and the evolution of the investment.

The Performance Lab page shows how positions performed over a chosen period, compared with the S&P 500 and NASDAQ 100, and what moves the portfolio stocks had in that interval.

On the Stocks page you can add or remove the stocks you are interested in and see all the current information about a stock.

The Stocks Performance page shows the top performing stocks in the market: the ones you hold, the ones on your watchlist and the ones you don't hold but are in the rankings, displayed by sector or overall.

Investment theses and data management

For each company you can save an investment thesis, with price thresholds and indicators, easy to follow. Based on the active theses, the alerts section shows which stocks have dropped below the fundamental Stop-Loss, below Fair Value or above the Target Price.

Positions, dividends and other operations, cash flow and investment theses all have full add, edit and delete operations, plus search filters. Chart and table colors can be changed, and columns can be hidden or pinned so they stay visible no matter how much you scroll.

From Export data you make a backup, and import works both from a backup and from the Excel files you used before. You can check whether the portfolio matches the file exactly, or import only what is new, for closed and open positions, dividends, cash flow or investment theses, however and whatever you want. If you run the same import often, you can save a template and no longer configure everything from scratch.

Every change in a portfolio is recorded in Log info, so it can be reviewed by both the user and the admins.

Roles and support

Users have the roles User, Admin and Superadmin. The Superadmin role can only be granted and revoked directly from the database. Anyone who needs help opens a ticket, and only the admin who takes it can talk to that user or log into their account to help with changes. Admins and superadmins have a shared chat and private one-to-one chats. I built this for people who need guidance in using the application.

Low resource usage

The application will run on a VPS with limited resources, so I focused on low consumption. Financial data is kept in a cache and is only updated when a user presses Refresh market data. The update is done for all users at once and everyone is notified. At this stage, small price differences are not worth the resources consumed by constantly displayed live prices.

Technologies used and why I chose them

Python with FastAPI for the backend. Python has the libraries the application needed: yfinance for market data, openpyxl for Excel import and export, ReportLab and Plotly for the PDF report and its charts. FastAPI automatically validates the data going in and out of the API. The frontend communicates only through this API, so all the financial logic lives in a single place. Money amounts are calculated with Decimal, not float, to avoid rounding errors.

React and TypeScript for the frontend. Tables with pinned columns, bulk editing, filters and interactive charts call for an interface built from components. TypeScript checks at compile time that the data received from the API has the expected shape. Components are reused: for example, the alerts panel is the same on Home and on Invest Strategy. The charts are built with Recharts.

PostgreSQL for data. When multiple users write at the same time, you need transactions and rules enforced by the database. An import cannot create duplicates in a portfolio, and if two admins take the same ticket in the same second, only one succeeds. The schema is versioned with Alembic, so any database change is a controlled migration.

Docker for running the app. The application runs the same locally and on the VPS: the database, the backend and the frontend, served through nginx, start together with the same configuration.

Market data cache, without Redis. For a single server, a local cache is enough. Redis would have been one more service to maintain on a VPS with limited resources. I will only consider it if the application needs multiple servers.

The project started as a Streamlit application with SQLite, suitable for a single user. When the application became multi-user, I moved it to the current architecture.

Next improvements

  • automatic portfolio import from Dropbox;
  • imports tailored for the files downloaded from brokers such as XTB, Tradeville and Interactive Brokers;
  • a mobile-friendly version and an improved front-end, on both mobile and desktop;
  • custom information for certain stocks in the portfolio, for example changing the sector a stock belongs to;
  • an Analytics page that is as easy to customize as possible;
  • sending the PDF report by email, with the chosen portfolio information;
  • automatically generated backups sent to a chosen email address;
  • email notifications when investment thesis alerts are activated, deactivated or changed;
  • the live launch, so the application can be used by users.

#Python #React #PostgreSQL
